summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old man with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis, chronic pain, and substance use was admitted for altered mental status and abdominal pain while intoxicated. He was managed in the ICU for alcohol and opioid withdrawal, receiving a phenobarbital load and methadone taper. Imaging revealed a new T5 vertebral compression fracture of indeterminate cause and cirrhosis with varices but no acute abdominal pathology. Liver enzymes were elevated with markedly increased GGT, suggesting ongoing alcoholic hepatitis, though steroids were not initiated due to a discriminant function of 11.4. He improved clinically, with resolution of withdrawal symptoms and stabilization of liver function. He was discharged home on a tapering methadone regimen, acamprosate, and standard cirrhosis medications, with plans for outpatient endoscopy, liver MRI, vitamin D follow-up, and enrollment in a recovery program.
problems: Unspecified fracture of T5-T6 vertebra, initial encounter for closed fracture

Exposure to other specified factors, initial encounter
